Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, a 14-track solo album that follows 2023's *Rocket Power*. The earlier record stayed close to the grief after Takeoff's death. *QRÖMELIFE* still returns to Takeoff, but it is less confined by mourning. Brighter records, harder club moments, a reunion with Offset and a new focus on fatherhood sit alongside the loss instead of being pulled back toward it.

The title comes from his word "qrome," which he links to "chromosome." He uses it to describe carrying something difficult while still getting up and doing what the day requires. His example is ordinary: something can happen to you and the next morning you still have to go to work. In that sense, qrome is not a recovery story. The difficult thing remains part of you, but it does not stop the rest of life from continuing.

Working with Pharrell Williams pushed him back toward the melodic side of his voice. In interviews about the album, he has talked about recovering the flexibility that let him move between Migos records, solo singles and pop features without sounding trapped in one mode. "Trance (Walk It Down)" shows that side clearly, with a looser delivery than the heavier material on *Rocket Power*. Other tracks move back toward harder drums, so the album does not stay in one emotional or musical register.

[apple:album:6809921222]

"Away" brings Offset back onto a Quavo record after the split that fractured Migos before Takeoff's death. The two repaired their relationship in the years that followed. Quavo described the session as therapeutic and compared it to being back in the school cafeteria with someone he has known since seventh grade. They are also sorting through new Migos music. He has said anything released under the name would need to honor Takeoff and benefit his estate, rather than simply presenting Migos as a duo.

Fatherhood changes the context again. Quavo became a father for the first time to a daughter and has said the role changed what he is working for. His own father died when he was four. He has said he wants to be present for every stage of his daughter's life, something he did not have growing up. The short film released with the album closes on him holding his daughter. *Rocket Power* was written from the position of someone grieving a member of his family. On *QRÖMELIFE*, he is also writing as someone responsible for raising a child.
